newsitem.title: USA: Freeport awaits results of Busang assays.
newsitem.headline: Freeport awaits results of Busang assays.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc hopes an independent assessment due out later this week will resolve conflicting estimates of gold reserves at the Busang find in Indonesia, Chairman Jim Bob Moffett said on Tuesday.

Freeport, which was selected to operate the prospect in East Kalimantan province, in late March said it found insignificant amounts of gold at the Busang site in contrast to Bre-X Minerals Ltd estimates of about 71 million ounces.

"That sampling will confirm what the drilling is from the additional six holes," he said of independent sampling tests being completed by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. "We're hoping that this new Strathcona drilling will add more light."

Freeport's findings, announced March 26, prompted Calgary- based Bre-X's decision to hire Strathcona to audit earlier drilling and sampling done by both companies and drill new core samples in the field.
"Freeport's participation is predicated on the fact that we will go forward and join only if we can confirm an economic deposit," Moffett said.

As operator of the Busang field, Freeport would have a 15 percent stake and pay up to $400 million to delineate reserves and build a mining complex to exploit reserves once estimated at $25 billion based on current gold prices.

In other business at the meeting, shareholders rejected a motion made by the Seattle Mennonite Church seeking to force the company to sever ties to the Indonesian military and allow independent environmental monitoring of its gold, copper and silver mining operations there.

The company for the second straight year was served with a civil lawsuit alleging human rights violations by the Indonesian military against villagers living near the company's Grasberg gold and copper mine in Irian Jaya province.

"This second lawsuit is another lawsuit that is an effort by several groups to intimidate and attempt to shake down the shareholders of the Freeport-McMoRan company because of the political agenda they have in Irian Jaya," Moffett said. The company earlier said it expected the lawsuit to be dismissed.

The meeting was held under tight security at the company's downtown New Orleans headquarters building, where shareholders were screened by metal detectors and reporters were sequestered in a separate room to view the proceedings on closed-circuit television.

Freeport is in the midst of a $960 million expansion of the company's ore grinding mill capacity in Indonesia is expected to boost production to about 200,000 metric tons per day in early 1998 from 125,000 metric tons per day currently, Moffett said.
